title: AI provider attempts
definition: Count of AI provider attempts (one per request sent to a model, image, voice or evaluation provider; not user actions) whose start falls in [start, end), with ok / failed / rate-limited / timeout / cancelled / unknown-outcome counts in measures. Retries and fallbacks are separate attempts. cost_basis says how each attempt's cost is known: reported (provider or gateway), price_table (computed from a versioned price table when recorded) or unknown.
limitations: Collected from the 058 deployment on (no backfill): not_instrumented before the first attempt, then collectingSince, and an interval that starts earlier is partial. Recording is best-effort (a failed write is skipped, never retried), so counts can fall short of provider bills.

title: AI tokens by type
definition: Sum of tokens of text attempts in [start, end) by token_type: input (input tokens not served from cache; all input tokens when the provider did not report cached tokens), cached (cached input tokens), output (output excluding reasoning) and reasoning. Provider input counts include cached tokens and output counts include reasoning (OpenAI semantics, PRD 8.0), so the four types partition an attempt's tokens.
limitations: An attempt whose provider did not report a token type counts as coverage unknown for that type (never zero); cached tokens are often unreported on gateway routes. Image and voice attempts are not token attempts.

title: AI attempt latency (p50 / p95)
definition: Per group, the 95th percentile (value) and the median (measures.p50Ms) of request-to-answer latency of provider attempts in [start, end), computed with percentile_cont over the group's attempts. Percentiles are never averaged across groups or periods.
limitations: Groups with fewer than 30 attempts carry reason small_sample (sampleCount is n). Total latency only (no first-token latency); voice sessions are excluded.

title: AI fallback and retry rate
definition: Attempts in [start, end) that ran on a fallback route or were a retry (attempt number above 1) divided by all attempts; fallback and retry counts and rates separately in measures.
limitations: Retries made inside a provider SDK are invisible; growth retries are numbered per task, workspace and subject.

title: AI cost per provider attempt
definition: Mean recorded cost (micro-USD) of attempts in [start, end) whose cost is known: provider-reported, or computed at write time from the versioned price table named on the attempt; refused attempts cost 0. Attempts with unknown cost are coverage unknown and excluded from the mean.
limitations: Attempt costs are never re-priced; the canonical spend remains ai_cost_actual over the ledger. Price tables bill cached input at the input price (no cached rate recorded).

title: AI cost per useful outcome
definition: Canonical AI cost of the period (actual settled ledger cost, failed and cancelled work included) divided by the useful outcomes of the same period and workspaces, from the proxy named in measures.basis: Time Back accepted outcomes (accepted drafts and adaptations, verified publications, activated automations; the default) or learning-event approvals and publishes (outcome_proxy). A period without outcomes is not_applicable, never zero.
limitations: A proxy, not a usefulness rating: cost and outcomes are matched by period and workspace, not by task. Learning events expire after 180 days. Unsettled cost rows make the ratio partial.

title: AI cost month-end forecast (scenario)
definition: Scenario, not a measurement: month-end AI cost for the local calendar month containing the interval end = month-to-date actual ledger cost plus an ordinary least-squares line through the 56 complete local days before as-of, extrapolated over the rest of the month (today counts as the larger of its actual so far and the line; negative days floor at zero). With window: the cumulative cost per day of the month (measures.kind actual or projection). measures name the basis ('scenario'), method, slope and the global monthly budget.
limitations: insufficient_history until 56 complete days of ledger history exist. A straight line ignores launches, pricing changes and seasonality; the budget line is shown only where a global monthly budget exists.
